title: Genomic data need a stronger equity framework | Science
description: In June 2026, the US Fish and Wildlife Service signed a memorandum of understanding with Colossal Biosciences, a for-profit genetic engineering company, to biobank and sequence threatened and endangered species, including species foreign to the United States (1, 2). Commercial sequencing companies have also collaborated with academic researchers to publish whole-genome data from many nonhuman primate species (3), which have later been used to predict tolerated variation in the human genome (4). Whether held privately, as in the recent agreement, or released openly, as required for peer-reviewed journal articles, genomes of endangered wildlife accrue commercial value for years after any conservation use has ended, with no guaranteed returns to the communities or national institutions in the source countries that protect the species. To ensure equitable benefit sharing, the terms of genome commercialization should be set before sequence data are generated.
